---
title: "About"
description: "Why this publication exists and how to scrutinize its work."
---

The Public Record is a starter publication for evidence-led investigations of public data. Its central rule is simple: a reader should be able to trace every published claim back to a source and inspect every consequential transformation.

The finished article is only one view of the work. The repository also preserves the source snapshot, retrieval details, cleaning and analysis code, assumptions, limitations, and revision history.

## Contact and corrections

Corrections can be proposed through the [public GitHub repository](https://github.com/paul-j-hamilton/public-data-investigations/issues). A correction should identify what changed, when it changed, and whether the change affected the article's conclusions. Material corrections belong both on the article and in the repository history.

## Licensing

Unless an investigation says otherwise, original writing is intended for release under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and original code under the [MIT License](https://opensource.org/license/mit). Third-party data retains its original terms.
